high.title: DSC CEO: VN-Index Correction Phases Could Be Very "Deep and Painful" if They Occur
high.summary: At DSC's AGM on April 16, CEO Bach Quoc Vinh projected VN-Index could reach 1,950-2,000 points in a positive scenario, driven by strong economic growth targeting ~10% GDP, easing US-Iran tensions, and stabilizing energy prices. Market support comes from expected 10-15% pre-tax profit growth of listed companies and attractive P/E valuations at ~11x. The market upgrade story could attract $5-8 billion in foreign capital. However, Vinh warned investors to monitor risks including prolonged geopolitical tensions, inflation pressure, and high interest rates and exchange rates. While long-term prospects are positive, he emphasized caution as any market corrections could be "deep and painful." This assessment is crucial for VND traders as it highlights both upside potential and significant downside risks, particularly around FX and rate pressures that could trigger sharp corrections.

high.title: Foreign Investors "Dump" Nearly 40,000 Billion VND of Vietnamese Stocks Since Year-Start
high.summary: Foreign investors continue massive outflows from Vietnamese markets, selling net nearly 40,000 billion VND in just over 4 months of 2026, despite the market upgrade news. VCBF's portfolio manager Nguyen Duy Anh explained this reflects global capital flow shifts, with investors pulling out of high-risk markets to return to the US. High US interest rates make domestic investment more attractive than overseas allocation. When compared to markets like Vietnam, investors face additional FX risk that significantly reduces relative attractiveness. This sustained outflow pattern represents a major headwind for VND and Vietnamese assets, as foreign capital flight puts downward pressure on the currency and reduces liquidity in domestic markets. The trend suggests structural challenges for Vietnam in attracting foreign investment amid high US rates.

high.title: Oil Prices Plunge Over 11% as Iran Reports Good News from Hormuz Strait
high.summary: Oil prices crashed over 11% on Friday after Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced Hormuz Strait is "completely open" during the ceasefire period, easing supply disruption fears. WTI crude for May delivery fell over 11% to around $84/barrel, while Brent for June dropped over 10% to around $89/barrel. This reflects investor expectations that supply will gradually resume if regional tensions continue cooling. The strait's reopening is crucial as about one-fifth of global crude flows through this chokepoint. For VND traders, lower oil prices could ease Vietnam's import bill and reduce inflationary pressures, potentially providing room for more accommodative monetary policy. However, the dramatic price swing also highlights ongoing volatility in commodity markets that could impact Vietnam's terms of trade.

medium.title: Q1 2026 Securities Firm Update: First Hundred-Billion Loss Emerges
medium.summary: Among 12 securities firms reporting Q1 results, EVS Securities posted the first major loss of hundreds of billions VND. Revenue collapsed 91% YoY to just 8 billion VND, while operating costs surged to 188 billion VND. In contrast, Agriseco saw revenue rise 39% to 145 billion VND with pre-tax profit up 35% to 55 billion VND. This divergence reflects varying business models and market positioning amid volatile conditions.

medium.title: Gold Prices Reverse Course on April 17 Afternoon
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices reversed higher by about 500,000 VND/tael in afternoon trading after three consecutive days of declines. SJC gold bars traded at 167.5-171.5 million VND/tael, while gold rings ranged 167.0-170.5 million VND/tael across major dealers. International spot gold stood at $4,783/ounce, showing the premium between domestic and international prices remains elevated.

medium.title: MB Bank Adjusts Interest Rates: Which Tenor Has Highest Rate?
medium.summary: MB Bank reduced deposit rates across most tenors, with 6-11 month rates down 0.1pp to ~4.6%, and 12-18 month rates down 0.2pp to ~6.3%. The 24-month tenor remains highest at 7.2% after a 0.3pp cut, while longer-term rates (36-60 months) fell 0.5pp to ~7.0%. The moves reflect banks adjusting to monetary policy and funding cost pressures, signaling potential broader rate environment changes.

medium.title: Iran Declares Full Opening of Hormuz Strait
medium.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister announced complete reopening of Hormuz Strait for commercial vessels during the ceasefire period, though ships must follow designated routes. President Trump thanked Iran but said US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains until a deal is reached. Oil prices fell over 10% below $90/barrel as about one-fifth of global crude previously transited this route before the conflict.
